# Plan: Payment Processing — Test Coverage

## Existing coverage and test infrastructure retained
This changes unit tests only; processPayment() production behavior stays as-is.
The Stripe adapter suite already covers network timeouts, card declines (402),
rate limits (429), and recovery when an initial 502 is followed by a successful
charge. Receipt-builder failure behavior has its own passing regression tests.
The payment test factory explicitly configures max_retries=1 and exposes the
Stripe mock call history. Its injected virtual sleeper records backoff without
real delays, so an exhausted 502 operation makes exactly two charge attempts.
These existing helpers and regression suites remain in use for this change.

## Existing behavior retained
A successful charge returns a receipt with chargeId copied from Stripe,
amountCents equal to the requested integer amount, and currency equal to
the requested currency. For a 1000-cent USD charge returning id ch_paid,
the receipt is { chargeId: "ch_paid", amountCents: 1000, currency: "USD" }.
On repeated 502 responses, max_retries=1 means two total charge attempts
separated by one recorded 100 ms backoff, followed by PaymentUnavailable.
These contracts are already implemented; this plan adds their unit coverage.

Stripe mock and virtual sleeper. Other tests and production code stay as-is.

   is planned for this test.

# Plan: Payment Processing — Test Coverage (CEO review working plan)

Source: `PLAN.md` @ `09c9995` on `main`. Review: `/plan-ceo-review`, mode HOLD SCOPE (explicit user instruction). Base branch: `main` (git-native fallback; no remote).

## Context
processPayment() already implements two contracts (successful receipt shape; 502 retry then PaymentUnavailable) but the unit suite does not pin them. This plan adds two unit tests in the existing processPayment suite, reusing the existing factory (max_retries=1), Stripe mock (exposes call history) and virtual sleeper (records backoff). No production code changes.

## Evidence status
- Repo under review contains only `PLAN.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. The processPayment suite, factory, Stripe mock, virtual sleeper and adapter tests are **stated by the plan, not verifiable in this checkout**. All "Current" values below are plan statements, marked (plan-stated).
- No design doc, handoff note, TODOS.md, prior learnings, or brain digests exist for this project.

## Stated limits (kept)
| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Files changed | 1 (existing processPayment spec file) | plan |
| New tests | 2 | plan |
| Production code changes | 0 | plan |
| max_retries | 1 → exactly 2 charge attempts on exhausted 502 | plan-stated factory config |
| Backoff | one recorded 100 ms sleep between attempts | plan-stated |
| Receipt contract | `{ chargeId: "ch_paid", amountCents: 1000, currency: "USD" }` | plan-stated |

## Step 0A — Premise challenge
1. Right problem? Yes: two implemented contracts have no unit coverage; pinning them is the smallest useful change. No alternative framing is simpler.
2. Outcome: a regression in receipt shape or retry/backoff behavior fails CI before it reaches a customer's charge. The plan reaches this only if the tests actually assert the contracts. As written, test 1 (`truthy`) and test 2 (`rejects with PaymentUnavailable` only) do not; they detect the code path existing, not the contract holding. That is a proxy for coverage.
3. Do nothing: receipt-shape drift (e.g. amountCents returned as a string, currency dropped) and retry drift (3 attempts, 0 ms backoff, or no retry at all) all pass today's suite. The pain is real: these are money-path invariants.

## Step 0B — Existing code leverage
| Sub-problem | Existing code (plan-stated) | Reuse |
|---|---|---|
| Build a processPayment under test with deterministic retries | payment test factory, max_retries=1 | reuse as-is |
| Script Stripe responses / inspect calls | Stripe mock with call history | reuse; call history currently unused by the plan |
| Observe backoff without real delay | injected virtual sleeper with record | reuse; record currently unused by the plan |
| Adapter-level errors (timeout, 402, 429, 502-then-success) | Stripe adapter suite | already covered; do not duplicate |
| Receipt-builder failures | receipt-builder regression tests | already covered; do not duplicate |

Nothing is being rebuilt. The plan under-uses two helpers it already lists.

## Step 0C — Dream state
```
  CURRENT STATE                      THIS PLAN                        12-MONTH IDEAL
  Contracts implemented,    --->     2 tests in processPayment  --->  Every money-path contract
  no unit test pins them             suite; helpers reused             (shape, attempts, backoff,
  (drift is invisible)               (delta: +2 tests, 1 file)         error class) pinned by a
                                                                       deterministic unit test;
                                                                       drift fails CI, not prod.
```
The plan moves toward the ideal only if the tests pin the contracts. Weak assertions move sideways: they add test count without adding drift detection.

## Landscape check (Layer 1/2/3)
- Layer 1: inject the clock/sleeper, assert backend invocation count, assert the recorded delay schedule. Plan infrastructure already supports all three.
- Layer 2: current guidance agrees; source: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-08-14-test-jittered-retries-deterministically/view ("assert backend invocation count", "execute the logical schedule instantly and reproduce every decision").
- Layer 3: no eureka. Conventional wisdom is right here; the risk is under-asserting, not over-engineering.

## Step 0G — HOLD SCOPE checks
1. Complexity: 1 file, 0 new classes/services. Pass.
2. Minimum change for the goal: both tests are the goal; nothing is deferrable without abandoning it. No deferral question needed.
3. Stated invariants: the "Existing behavior retained" section states exact contracts. Tests that do not check them do not meet the plan's own acceptance criteria; repairing the assertions is in scope under HOLD SCOPE, but the plan explicitly chose "assert only", so each repair is asked as a separate row below.

D3 (ledger R1) — What should the successful-charge test assert?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-rQv537 on main; HOLD SCOPE review of the processPayment test-coverage plan.
ELI10: The plan states the exact receipt a 1000-cent USD charge must return ({ chargeId: "ch_paid", amountCents: 1000, currency: "USD" }), but test 1 only checks that *something* came back. A bug that returns {} or amountCents as "1000" (a string) or drops currency still passes. The factory already exposes the Stripe mock's call history and the sleeper's record, so checking them costs a few lines and no new helpers.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too weak and the money-path receipt can drift silently; a downstream ledger or invoice reads the wrong amount and the suite stays green.
Recommendation: A because the plan already wrote the contract down; asserting it is the whole point of the test and adds ~5 lines in the same file (human: ~15 min / CC: ~1 min).
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10
Net: same file, same effort tier; the choice is only how much drift the test can detect.

options.label: B) Receipt shape only
options.description: ✅ Pins chargeId, amountCents and currency exactly, catching the most likely regressions. ✅ Depends only on the return value, not on mock internals. ❌ A double Stripe call or an unexpected backoff on success would still pass unnoticed.

options.description: ✅ Matches the plan text exactly; zero change to the author's intent. ✅ Cannot break when receipt fields are added later. ❌ Passes on {} or any wrong amount/currency; it proves a return exists, not that the contract holds.
